## 固定收益開篇論點

8月10日美國公債收盤走勢，完全抹去上週五就業數據帶來的利率舒緩，能源通膨再度成為存續期間的眼前制約。2年期殖利率上升6個基點至4.25%，5年期上升6個基點至4.41%，10年期上升7個基點至4.72%，30年期上升6個基點至5.25%。這波近乎平行的賣壓使2s10s陡峭1個基點至47個基點，2s30s則維持100個基點不變。上週五的走勢延後市場對Fed緊縮時點的預期；週一則顯示，只要任何催化因素提高等待通膨降溫的代價，利率舒緩便可能迅速消退。

恢復荷姆茲海峽通航的努力未果，正是觸發市場轉向的催化因素。伊朗提出補償要求，與美國的直接協商又未取得進展，壓低市場對迅速復航的期待，Brent原油上漲4.94%至$87.68，WTI上漲5.01%至$82.10。實體供應限制不只反映在期貨市場，基準中東至中國航線的超大型油輪日租金已逼近$50萬。市場在7月CPI公布前重新計入能源價格傳導風險，10年期損益兩平通膨率擴大4個基點至2.29%，解釋名目殖利率漲幅的一半以上。

實質利率也同步上升，因此週一不能只解讀為油價衝擊。10年期實質殖利率上升3個基點至2.43%，回到8月6日水準，過去1個月累計上升11個基點。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack進一步強化政策面的壓力。她是7月主張升息、反對按兵不動的3位官員之一；她表示，目前利率並未明顯限制經濟，通膨不會自行回到2%，而單次升息25個基點恐怕不會有太大作用。她傾向升息若干次，但不預設最終利率，直接挑戰7月非農就業疲弱即可決定9月政策選擇的看法。

不過，這波賣壓仍然有序，並未演變成全面融資事件。S&P 500幾乎持平，VIX收於15.46，高收益債基金僅下跌約0.16%-0.17%。投資級債因存續期間較長，承受較大的按市價計算損失，但仍有19家公司發行合計$276億的美國高評級債券，發行人數創1月以來最多。這組訊號反映折現率升高、但市場承接功能正常，而非資本突然撤離。

週一走勢也凸顯官方壓低長天期殖利率的能力有限。美國財政部長Scott Bessent支持考慮調整發債年期結構，並採取措施降低日圓相關外溢效應；BMO調查中有61%的客戶預期，30年期公債標售規模下次調整將是縮減。這些預期仍未阻止30年期公債收於5.25%，較1個月前高19個基點。財政舉債、通膨公信力與海外相對價值的影響，仍大於美國財政部短期可用的政策訊號。

全球訊號帶來的是分化，而非緩解。日本央行新公布的7月會議摘要顯示，多位委員關注加快升息速度或擴大升息幅度；與此同時，日圓貶破159兌1美元，回吐干預帶動漲幅的一半。挪威核心通膨低於預期，中國消費者與生產者通膨普遍放緩，歐元區成長預估則因第2季表現較強而上調。這些發展為個別市場創造存續期間機會，也使政策路徑分歧，但仍不足以抵銷油價、Fed政策條件與偏高實質利率底部對美國收盤走勢的主導作用。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

各附息年期普遍重新定價，殖利率曲線僅溫和變動。2年期與5年期殖利率同升6個基點，10年期上升7個基點，30年期上升6個基點，壓力最大的是基準中期區段，但曲線中段並未明顯扭曲。2s10s僅擴大1個基點，2s30s維持100個基點。月度變化呈現更重要的斜率：2年期殖利率上升4個基點，5年期上升11個基點，10年期上升16個基點，30年期上升19個基點。週一近期政策風險升高，但累積負擔仍隨年期拉長而增加。

通膨補償主導當日走勢，與上週五由實質殖利率帶動的反彈形成鮮明對比。10年期名目殖利率上升7個基點，其中損益兩平通膨率擴大4個基點，實質殖利率上升3個基點。損益兩平通膨率收於2.29%，過去1個月上升5個基點；實質殖利率收於2.43%，過去1個月上升11個基點。能源因而重新推高市場要求的中期通膨溢價，投資人也繼續要求更高實質報酬，以補償政策、財政與供給的不確定性。兩者都未給Fed留下足夠空間，將招聘疲弱視為已足以約束經濟。

荷姆茲海峽連續第2個交易日改變近期通膨態勢。上週五非農就業衝擊一度將2年期殖利率壓低至4.19%，即使當時原油已上漲；週一兩大原油基準均上漲約5%，使2年期殖利率回升至4.25%，並帶動10年期殖利率超過8月6日收盤水準。談判未能恢復自由通航，美國總統Donald Trump拒絕伊朗的補償要求，水道營運摩擦成本仍異常高昂。傳導路徑並非美國需求轉強，而是實體能源風險先推升損益兩平通膨率，再影響市場對政策反應的預期。

Hammack把普遍的通膨持續性疑慮轉化為對政策幅度的明確判斷，使後續政策反應更受關注。她早在7月便主張升息並投下反對票；週一新增的訊息，是她認為升息1碼恐怕不會對經濟造成實質影響，可能需要升息若干次。她的判斷基於目前利率並未明顯限制經濟，且通膨不會自行收斂；但她拒絕指明最終利率。CPI因此仍可改變升息次數與時點，只是舉證責任已轉向能夠支持繼續耐心等待的數據。

7月非農就業萎縮仍是重要反向力量，但週一沒有新的政府就業數據公布。非農就業人數減少2.3萬，市場共識為增加8萬；最新分析指出，地方政府就業減少6萬，部分源於季節性因素，也與用來擴充教師編制的聯邦支援到期有關。過去3個月私人就業平均增加4萬，接近吸收新增勞動力所需約5萬人的粗略估計。這樣的組成顯示就業訊號嚴峻、但尚無定論：整體招聘疲弱，私人經濟卻比表面數字更接近吸收新增勞動力所需的速度。

這股張力說明為何賣壓未使殖利率曲線明顯趨平。若需求明確加速，壓力應集中於2年至5年期；若純屬財政公信力衝擊，長端應更明顯陡峭。實際上，能源推升整條曲線的通膨補償，Hammack則保留連續升息的可能。30年期殖利率為5.25%，10年期為4.72%，兩者也持續承受就業疲弱無法消除的供給溢價。

美國財政部的政策溝通只能局部壓抑這項溢價。措辭從評估未來增發，轉為評估未來調整，先前已打開縮減20年期與30年期標售規模的可能；目前BMO調查也顯示，多數受訪者預期下一次30年期發行規模將下調。但目前尚未宣布任何縮減。把融資轉向較短天期附息債，只會改變存續期間進入市場的位置，並不會消除舉債需求；持續的通膨與每年近$2兆的赤字，也限制僅靠年期管理壓低殖利率的空間。

當日交易相當活躍，但除價格走勢外，未顯示明確的單向資金流失衡。名目附息美國公債成交按原始面額計合計$6,980億，共261,262筆交易，其中7年至10年期區間為$1,571億，20年期以上為$625億。這些數字顯示，承擔主要存續期間風險的各區段均出現活躍賣壓。收盤價本身仍是更清楚的訊號：通膨補償與實質殖利率同步上升，在CPI與再融資標售前，前端與長端都未找到持久的抵銷力量。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

信用市場承受的利率衝擊，依存續期間長短呈現清楚梯度。LQD下跌0.55%，HYG下跌0.16%，JNK下跌0.17%。長天期美國AAA-A級與BBB級公司債指數分別下跌0.94%及0.86%，接近20年期以上美國公債指數的0.82%跌幅。這些表現主要反映基準殖利率上升造成的總報酬損失，而非投機級信用普遍惡化。長存續期間資產重新定價之際，初級發行市場仍然開放。

週一高評級發債日程的規模與廣度，使這股承接力更具意義。19家發行人合計發行$276億，發行人數創7個月新高，僅略低於1月5日的20筆交易。上週已有$800億債券完成定價，為2026年第3高單週發行量；借款人趕在本週通膨報告公布前加速發債。截至上週五，美國投資級債發行量已達$1.4兆，較2020年同期速度快9%；全球聯貸發行量則比先前紀錄提早1個多月突破$5兆。資本仍然充裕，但發行人把重大事件前的發債窗口視為稀缺資源。

IBM證明投資需求橫跨不同幣別與發行人題材。該公司發行C$27.5億、分為4年期與8年期的楓葉債，為14年來首次在加拿大市場發債。8年期券定價較基準高120個基點，較初步討論水準略窄；儘管IBM股價今年以來已下跌20%，投資人也擔心其基礎設施與軟體業務受壓，交易仍順利完成。這筆交易把觀察範圍擴大到美國超大規模雲端業者之外：只要年期與利差提供足夠補償，跨境高評級借款人仍可完成大額交易。

AI融資同時更深入槓桿貸款與特定資產結構。Lambda推出一筆$9.17億貸款，用於購置及安裝Nvidia GPU，預先行銷後訂單接近$20億。建議條件最高為基準利率加375個基點、發行價99，年期4.4年，約4年內全額攤還，並設有提前贖回罰則。這些保障可壓低技術快速汰換資產的再融資與展期風險，也顯示強勁需求來自交易結構，而非僅憑AI成長曝險。

Global AI另闢融資管道，取得JPMorgan主導、用於資料中心的$4.41億融資額度。這家成立2年的公司表示，已簽約收入達$62億，其中$10億來自已建成並交付的容量。這筆交易規模較小，且未提供定價，但收入支持使其有別於純投機性的產能計畫。結合Lambda的案例可見，貸款人會分別衡量已簽約用途、資產壽命、攤還與執行能力，而非把所有建設視為同質信用。

監管待遇可能擴大下一波供給。美國證券交易委員會工作人員上月底認定，與實體資料中心資產連結的一大類債券，無須遵循適用於傳統資產擔保交易的風險自留與揭露要求。這項指引並非正式修法，也不適用於以抵押貸款擔保的資料中心CMBS。不過，資料中心ABS年發行量已由2020年的$24億增至去年的$155億，今年可望再創新高；這項指引仍移除一項成本高昂的結構性限制。

供給能力擴大之際，Nvidia與大型另類資產管理公司正規劃規模達$5,000億的AI基礎設施合作案，已點名的參與者包括Apollo、Blackstone、BlackRock與Brookfield。龐大規模擴充投資管線，但在科技業反覆發債已使流通債券利差擴大之後，也進一步增加未來股債融資需求。週一半導體指數下跌2.94%，其中Nvidia下跌2.9%，顯示市場並未把這項融資消息視為毫無保留的利多。

信用市場的結論是流動性充裕，但投資人對保障條款與存續期間定價的要求日益明確。擁擠的高評級發債日程順利完成，IBM睽違14年再度取得外幣融資，Lambda訂單也超過擬貸款規模。然而，最具吸引力的條件來自攤還安排、利差與事件時點，而較寬鬆的證券化待遇預示供給增加。美國公債殖利率上升並未關閉市場，但交易結構、新券讓利，以及資金進入已經擁擠投資組合的先後順序，都變得更加重要。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

日本仍是最直接影響美國公債的海外傳導管道，因為貨幣政策正常化、財政供給與匯市干預目前相互強化。日本央行在7月30日至31日會議維持政策利率於1%，但週一公布的摘要顯示，委員更加重視通膨上行風險。一名委員表示，升息速度可能超過市場預期；另一名委員則主張應保留調整幅度的彈性，包括可能擴大單次調整幅度。會中僅高田創主張連續升息，但摘要顯示，疑慮並不限於這一張反對票。

政策反應函數已從推升基礎通膨至2%，轉向防止通膨向上偏離。一名委員指出，即使政策利率已達1%，仍低於日本央行估計的1.1%-2.5%中性區間。隔夜交換市場計入9月升息機率約三分之二，10月前升息機率則為96%。加快正常化會提高美國公債的相對價值門檻，也可能使日本資金留在國內，尤其美國長天期殖利率已因本國財政與通膨風險而上升。

匯率走勢顯示，干預尚未化解根本性的利差問題。日圓盤中低點貶幅超過1%，貶破159兌1美元，回吐7月31日美日聯合操作帶動漲幅的約一半。Bessent所指的外匯穩定基金規模不到$2,200億，相較之下，估計日本僅7月30日一天就投入$530億。FIMA附買回機制可讓日本把超過$1兆的美國公債部位部分轉為美元現金，無須直接賣出；但近期公布的數據顯示，日本並未動用該機制。

財政政策使日本央行與匯率問題更為複雜。經濟財政政策擔當大臣城內實為一項計畫辯護，主張未來14年向關鍵產業投入370兆日圓，並實施為期2年、估計每年約5兆日圓的消費稅減稅。他認為，生產力提高與日圓資產需求增加將改善財政永續性；他也支持日本央行獨立性，且不反對提早升息。公私部門的資金分攤尚未說明，因此這項計畫可望支持長期成長，但短期內仍保留JGB供給與國內買盤的不確定性。壽險負債管道使這個買方基礎在邊際上更為脆弱。日本壽險業2026年前5個月支付給解約保戶的款項年增約40%，超過JPY6兆、約$380億，原因是BOJ緊縮後出現更多高收益替代資產。Meiji Yasuda第1季保費收入也下降28%至JPY7,937億。保險公司通常持有JGB以配對長期負債，但解約加速可能把未實現債券損失轉成現金需求，使其在殖利率上升時反而更難增加存續期間。

北歐通膨走勢相反。挪威7月不含能源的核心CPI維持在2.7%，低於市場共識2.9%及挪威央行6月預估的3.3%。隔夜交換市場將本週會議的升息定價由6個基點降至2個基點，但截至9月仍計入15個基點，且國內生產的商品與服務價格加速。受電價影響，整體通膨升至3.0%，高於市場共識2.8%。這樣的組合大幅削弱立即升息的理由，但秋季政策路徑仍未底定。

丹麥整體通膨降溫更為明確，7月通膨率由1.9%降至1.7%。中國則呈現更廣泛的減速：CPI年增率由1%降至0.5%，生產者通膨由4.1%放緩至3.5%。中國政策性銀行5年期以上債券指數上漲0.05%，與美國及其他已開發市場美元存續期間資產普遍下跌形成對比。這些在地結果支撐各自殖利率曲線的需求，但分化也降低市場對全球政策週期同步的期待。

羅馬尼亞顯示，歐洲政策分歧不只存在於歐元區內部。油價與受管制價格效應使5月與6月通膨升至10%以上，央行因而把基準利率維持在6.5%，是EU最高水準。利率已近2年未變；政治爭議同時延後解鎖EU資金所需的改革。Moody's把主權評等維持在最低投資等級，主要評級機構仍因政府運作與赤字削減能力給予負向展望。羅馬尼亞本地債與美元債上漲，但評級暫時過關，並未消除通膨下降與財政措施落實後才能寬鬆的限制。歐元區成長韌性為海外存續期間再加上一項限制條件。調查將2026年成長預測由0.5%上調至0.8%，幾乎完全因第2季GDP成長0.4%，為預期速度的2倍。第3季預測維持0.2%，其後僅逐步改善。經濟活動實際表現較強，降低眼前的衰退壓力；但前瞻預估未變，加上能源成本再度上升，仍不足以推論歐洲正進入需求明顯升溫的格局。海外因素對美國公債的淨影響，仍是日本資產競爭與部分市場高利率延續，由其他地區選擇性通膨降溫加以抵銷，而非全球同步追捧存續期間。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

共同衝擊對新興市場美元債略為不利。美元指數上漲0.19%至99.79，EMB下跌0.42%，15年期以上新興市場美元主權債指數下跌0.29%。美國實質殖利率上升、美元走強，加上油價上漲約5%，共同提高硬通貨借款人的折現率，但市場走勢遠非全面清算。對最脆弱的發行人而言，在地通膨曝險與融資結構仍比指數變動更為重要。

菲律賓凸顯石油進口國在成長疲弱時面臨的政策限制。菲律賓央行總裁Eli Remolona表示，央行準備採取一切必要的緊縮措施，使通膨回到目標；此前第2季經濟成長意外放緩至2.3%，消費與投資均萎縮。通膨率為6.2%，超過政府目標的2倍，但經濟放緩降低立即行動的壓力，副總裁Zeno Abenoja也表示核心通膨可能已觸頂。因此，當地存續期間面臨的是停滯性通膨取捨，而非對經濟活動轉弱的直接反應。

Braskem的案例顯示，與主權國家的關聯會使公司信用風險更複雜，卻不會將其消除。包括Elliott與Contrarian在內的債權人，要求國營Petrobras在Braskem於8月24日庭外重整期限前，提供股權、營運資金或次順位債。Petrobras一直抗拒，部分原因是避免增加持股並可能併表Braskem的債務。為避免進入司法重整，必須取得至少三分之一債權人的支持；Moody's已將現有法院暫緩令視為違約。2030年到期債券的利差約為美國公債加1,900個基點。

Chile選擇透過明確的主權資本移轉，降低另一家國營企業的債務風險。政府允許Codelco留存2025年全部$24.2億獲利，是公司逾50年歷史上首次保留單一年度100%盈餘。Codelco負債約$250億、創歷史新高，產量則接近28年低點；留存現金的目的，是在不進一步舉債下支應復甦。公司仍須把銷售額的10%繳給國家，因此政府是以當期財政收入換取更強的準主權資產負債表，也要求公司更嚴格安排投資優先順序。Braskem案適逢巴西選舉年，同樣具有政治敏感性，但相關負債仍是公司債務，而非巴西主權債。債權人反提案提高達成庭外協議的可能性，但Petrobras不願介入，凸顯相反的風險移轉選擇：保護Braskem可能把槓桿或資本需求轉向國營股東。Codelco已取得明確的盈餘留存緩衝，Braskem則仍未就股東支持的形式與規模達成協議；期限、所需債權人門檻及任何股東出資，仍是後續最重要的檢驗條件。相較整體新興市場指數溫和的單日變動，這些差異更為重要。

## 跨資產

跨資產走勢驗證通膨與地緣政治重新定價，但未顯示經濟成長普遍轉折向下。WTI收於$82.10，Brent收於$87.68，兩者均上漲約5%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升4個基點。S&P 500僅下跌0.06%，VIX雖上升3.76%，仍處於受控的15.46。能源與政策溢價明確升高，但名目經濟活動風險仍有限，等待通膨降溫的成本則已上升。

科技股是風險趨避較明顯的區塊。Nasdaq 100下跌0.34%，半導體指數下跌2.94%；規模$5,000億的基礎設施合作案曝光後，Nvidia下跌2.9%。融資承諾支撐長期產能需求，但投資人對循環融資與更龐大資本需求的疑慮，壓抑相關股票的受益空間。這波反應也呼應信用市場對AI相關債務的要求，包括攤還、擔保品及新券讓利。

儘管美元走強、10年期實質殖利率上升，黃金仍上漲2.69%至$4,457.50，顯示地緣政治與制度性避險需求延續。美元升幅不大，過去1個月仍下跌1.17%，因此本交易日並非美元流動性衝擊。以總報酬計，高收益債表現也優於投資級長存續期間債券。油價、金價與半導體股共同凸顯核心張力：通膨與融資風險升高，但整體股市與投機級信用條件仍正常運作。

## 前瞻市場意涵

週三公布的7月CPI，必須判斷週一能源衝擊能否推翻就業數據造成的Fed緊縮定價延後。市場預期中位數為整體CPI月增0.1%，前值為下降0.4%；核心CPI預期月增0.2%、年增2.5%。若數據接近或低於上述水準，尤其服務價格未出現普遍壓力，將削弱Hammack所稱需要連續升息的論點，也可能回吐2年期殖利率6個基點升幅的一部分。若數據明顯高於預期，或荷姆茲海峽持續受阻，使運費與原油維持在週一附近水準，則會把能源衝擊連結至更廣泛的通膨過程，讓9月決策重新成為殖利率曲線焦點。

規模$1,250億的再融資標售，將檢驗目前殖利率提供的補償是否充分，以及長端承接風險是否仍未解決。週二$580億的3年期標售檢驗重新定價後的政策路徑，週三$420億的10年期標售檢驗實質殖利率2.43%附近的需求，週四$250億的30年期標售則檢驗收盤殖利率5.25%附近的財政存續期間風險。非交易商承接均衡、次級市場殖利率穩定，將顯示即使未來尚未縮減長天期發行，目前殖利率也足以吸收已公告供給。若出現標售尾差、交易商承接集中或標售後曲線再度陡峭，便表示對未來縮減長債規模的期待不足以抵銷當前融資需求；日圓若再度貶破160兌1美元，則會加劇海外需求疑慮。

本週AI交易將揭示，週一擁擠的高評級發債日程與Lambda預先行銷訂單，代表持久承接能力，還是僅限於特定條件的需求。Lambda承諾截止日為週四，最終利差、發行價格，以及是否保留4.4年期全額攤還結構，是最清楚的槓桿貸款觀察指標。下一筆資料中心ABS或公司債，也將顯示SEC待遇放寬能否在不迫使流通科技債提供更多讓利的情況下擴大供給。若交易以接近建議條件完成，且次級市場債券穩定，壓力將持續集中於結構與存續期間；若訂單轉弱、定價擴大或配售後出現損失，龐大投資管線便會演變為企業融資成本更廣泛的上升。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 10 Treasury close erased Friday's labor-led reprieve and re-established energy inflation as the immediate constraint on duration. The 2-year yield rose 6 basis points to 4.25%, the 5-year added 6 basis points to 4.41%, the 10-year increased 7 basis points to 4.72%, and the 30-year climbed 6 basis points to 5.25%. The nearly parallel selloff left 2s10s 1 basis point steeper at 47 basis points and 2s30s unchanged at 100. Friday had pushed the expected timing of Federal Reserve restraint outward; Monday showed that the relief was vulnerable to any catalyst that raises the inflation cost of waiting.

The failed effort to restore passage through the Strait of Hormuz supplied that catalyst. Brent rose 4.94% to $87.68 and WTI gained 5.01% to $82.10 as Iran's compensation demands and the lack of direct progress with the US dimmed expectations of a quick reopening. The physical constraint was visible beyond futures: the cost of hiring a supertanker on the benchmark Middle East-to-China route approached $500,000 a day. The 10-year breakeven widened 4 basis points to 2.29%, accounting for more than half of the nominal move, as the market repriced a renewed energy pass-through before July CPI.

Real rates also rose, preventing a simple reading of the session as an oil-only shock. The 10-year real yield increased 3 basis points to 2.43%, matching its August 6 level and leaving it 11 basis points higher over 1 month. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack reinforced that policy component. One of the three officials who dissented against July's hold in favor of an increase, she said rates were not meaningfully restricting the economy, inflation would not return to 2% on its own, and one 25-basis-point move probably would not do much. Her preference for some number of increases, without prejudging the endpoint, directly challenged the idea that weak July payrolls settle the September decision.

The selloff was nevertheless orderly and did not become a generalized funding event. The S&P 500 was almost unchanged, the VIX closed at 15.46, and high-yield funds fell only about 0.16%-0.17%. Investment-grade duration carried more of the mark-to-market loss, yet 19 companies still sold $27.6 billion of US high-grade bonds, the busiest issuer count since January. That combination points to a higher discount-rate regime with functioning absorption, not an abrupt withdrawal of capital.

Monday also exposed the limits of official efforts to contain long yields. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has supported possible changes to the maturity mix and steps intended to reduce yen-related spillover; 61% of clients in a BMO poll expected the next move in 30-year auction sizes to be a decrease. Those expectations did not stop the long bond from closing at 5.25%, 19 basis points above its month-earlier level. Fiscal borrowing, inflation credibility and foreign relative value remain larger than the near-term signaling tools available to Treasury.

Global evidence added dispersion rather than relief. A newly released summary of the Bank of Japan's July meeting showed several members focused on faster or larger increases, even as the yen weakened past 159 per dollar and erased half of its intervention-led rally. Norway's core inflation undershot expectations, China recorded a broad moderation in consumer and producer inflation, and euro-area growth estimates improved on a stronger Q2. These developments create local duration opportunities and competing policy paths, but they do not offset a US close dominated by oil, Fed conditionality and a high real-rate floor.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The repricing was broad across coupon maturities, with only modest curve movement. Equal 6-basis-point increases at 2 and 5 years, a 7-basis-point move at 10 years and 6 basis points at 30 years put the largest pressure in the benchmark intermediate sector without producing a distinctive belly distortion. The 2s10s curve widened just 1 basis point, and 2s30s remained at 100. Monthly changes preserve the more important slope: yields are 4 basis points higher at 2 years, 11 at 5 years, 16 at 10 years and 19 at 30 years. Near-term policy risk rose Monday, but the accumulated burden still increases with maturity.

Inflation compensation led the daily move, in sharp contrast with Friday's real-yield-led rally. The 10-year nominal yield rose 7 basis points as its breakeven widened 4 basis points and its real yield increased 3. The breakeven's 2.29% close is 5 basis points higher over 1 month; the 2.43% real yield is 11 basis points higher. Energy therefore reopened a medium-term inflation premium, while investors continued to demand a larger real return for policy, fiscal and supply uncertainty. Neither component gave the Fed room to treat weak hiring as sufficient restraint.

Hormuz changed the immediate inflation state for a second consecutive session. Friday's payroll shock had pulled the 2-year yield to 4.19% even as crude rose; Monday's roughly 5% advance in both oil benchmarks restored the 2-year to 4.25% and carried the 10-year above its August 6 close. Negotiations had not produced free passage, President Donald Trump rejected Iran's compensation demands, and the waterway's operating friction remained unusually costly. The transmission ran from physical energy risk into breakevens and then into the expected policy response, rather than through evidence of stronger US demand.

Hammack made that response more consequential because she converted a general persistence concern into a statement about scale. She had already dissented in July in favor of an increase; Monday's delta was her judgment that one quarter-point move probably would not materially affect the economy and that some number may be required. Her view rests on rates not being meaningfully restrictive and inflation not converging on its own. The qualification is that she declined to specify the endpoint. CPI can therefore alter the number and timing, but the burden has shifted toward data that justify continued patience.

The July payroll contraction remains an important counterforce, although Monday supplied no new government labor release. Payrolls fell 23,000 against an 80,000 consensus, and a current analysis identified a 60,000 decline in local-government employment as partly seasonal and tied to expiring federal support for expanded teaching staffs. Private payrolls averaged 40,000 over the past 3 months, close to a rough 50,000 estimate of the pace needed to absorb new labor-force entrants. That composition makes the labor signal serious but not conclusive: total hiring is weak, yet the private economy is nearer replacement pace than the headline implies.

This tension explains why the selloff did not materially flatten the curve. A clear acceleration in demand would have concentrated pressure at 2 to 5 years; a pure fiscal credibility shock would have steepened the long end more visibly. Instead, energy raised inflation compensation across the curve while Hammack protected the option of repeated tightening. The 30-year at 5.25% and the 10-year at 4.72% also remain exposed to a supply premium that weak labor cannot remove.

Treasury's communication offers only a partial cap on that premium. The shift from evaluating future issuance increases to evaluating future changes had already opened the possibility of smaller 20- and 30-year auctions, and the BMO poll now shows a majority expecting the next 30-year size move to be down. No reduction has been announced. Redirecting financing toward shorter coupons would change where duration enters the market, not eliminate the borrowing need, while persistent inflation and nearly $2 trillion annual deficits limit how far maturity management alone can lower yields.

The day's trading activity was substantial without revealing a directional flow imbalance beyond the observed price move. Nominal Treasury coupon activity totaled $698.0 billion in original-face value across 261,262 trades, including $157.1 billion in the 7- to 10-year bucket and $62.5 billion beyond 20 years. Those figures describe an active selloff across the sectors carrying the main duration burden. The close itself remains the cleaner signal: inflation compensation and real yields both rose, and neither the front end nor the long end found a durable offset before CPI and the refunding auctions.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Credit absorbed the rates shock with a clear duration gradient. LQD fell 0.55%, compared with declines of 0.16% in HYG and 0.17% in JNK. Long-maturity US AAA-A and BBB corporate bond indices lost 0.94% and 0.86%, respectively, close to the 0.82% decline in the 20-year-plus Treasury index. The evidence is primarily a total-return effect from higher benchmark yields, not a broad deterioration in speculative credit. Primary issuance remained open even as long-duration assets repriced.

The scale and breadth of Monday's high-grade calendar make that absorption meaningful. Nineteen issuers sold a combined $27.6 billion, the largest issuer count in 7 months and just below the 20 deals seen on January 5. Borrowers accelerated ahead of this week's inflation reports after $80 billion priced last week, the third-highest weekly total of 2026. US investment-grade issuance had reached $1.4 trillion by Friday, 9% ahead of the comparable 2020 pace, and global syndicated issuance crossed $5 trillion more than a month earlier than the previous record. Capital remains available, but issuers are treating event windows as scarce.

IBM demonstrated that the bid extends across currencies and issuer narratives. It sold C$2.75 billion of 4- and 8-year Maple bonds in its first Canadian transaction in 14 years. The 8-year tranche priced 120 basis points above its benchmark, slightly tighter than initial discussion, despite a 20% year-to-date equity decline and investor concern about pressure on its infrastructure and software businesses. The result broadens the evidence beyond US hyperscalers: cross-border high-grade borrowers can clear sizable transactions when maturity and spread offer adequate compensation.

AI financing is simultaneously moving deeper into leveraged loans and asset-specific structures. Lambda launched a $917 million loan to fund Nvidia GPUs and installation, with orders nearing $2 billion after premarketing. The proposed terms were as much as 375 basis points over the benchmark at 99, with a 4.4-year maturity, full amortization over roughly 4 years and an early-redemption penalty. Those protections compress refinancing and extension risk around assets with rapid technological turnover. They also show that strong demand is being purchased with structure, not simply with exposure to AI growth.

Global AI added another financing channel by raising a $441 million JPMorgan-led facility for data centers. The two-year-old company cited $6.2 billion of contracted revenue, including $1 billion of capacity already built and delivered. The transaction is smaller and its pricing was not supplied, but the revenue backing distinguishes it from a purely speculative capacity plan. Together with Lambda, it shows lenders separating contracted use, asset life, amortization and execution rather than treating the buildout as one homogeneous credit.

Regulatory treatment may expand the next wave of supply. SEC staff concluded late last month that a major subset of bonds tied to physical data-center assets does not have to follow risk-retention and disclosure requirements applied to conventional asset-backed deals. The guidance is not a formal rule change and does not extend to data-center CMBS backed by mortgages. It nonetheless removes a costly structural constraint from a sector whose annual ABS issuance grew to $15.5 billion last year from $2.4 billion in 2020 and is on pace for another record.

That capacity increase arrives as Nvidia and large alternative-asset managers plan a $500 billion AI-infrastructure partnership. Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock and Brookfield are among the named participants. The size reinforces the investment pipeline, but it also enlarges the future debt and equity funding requirement after recurring technology issuance had already widened seasoned bonds. Monday's 2.94% decline in the semiconductor index, including a 2.9% fall in Nvidia, shows that the financing announcement was not received as an unqualified increase in value.

The credit conclusion is abundant liquidity with increasingly explicit investor protection and duration pricing. A crowded high-grade calendar cleared, IBM accessed a foreign currency after 14 years, and Lambda drew orders exceeding the proposed loan size. Yet the strongest terms were attached to amortization, spread and event timing, while easier securitization treatment promises more supply. Higher Treasury yields are not closing markets; they are increasing the importance of structure, concession and the sequence in which capital reaches already crowded portfolios.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Japan remains the most direct foreign transmission channel into Treasuries because monetary normalization, fiscal supply and currency intervention now reinforce one another. The BOJ held its policy rate at 1% at the July 30-31 meeting, but Monday's summary showed members placing greater weight on upside inflation risk. One participant said the pace of increases could exceed market expectations; another urged flexibility over the size of a move, including potentially larger adjustments. Only Hajime Takata had called for a back-to-back increase at the meeting, yet the summary revealed broader concern than that single dissent.

The reaction function has shifted from lifting underlying inflation toward 2% to preventing an upward deviation. One member noted that the policy rate remains below the BOJ's estimated 1.1%-2.5% neutral range even after reaching 1%. Overnight swaps priced roughly a two-thirds chance of an increase in September and 96% by October. Faster normalization raises the relative-value hurdle for Treasuries and can retain Japanese capital at home, especially when US long yields are already responding to domestic fiscal and inflation risk.

Currency behavior shows that intervention has not resolved the underlying rate differential. The yen weakened more than 1% at its intraday low, traded beyond 159 per dollar and erased about half of the gain from the July 31 US-Japan operation. Bessent's dedicated Exchange Stabilization Fund holds less than $220 billion, compared with an estimated $53 billion spent by Japan on July 30 alone. The FIMA repo facility could turn part of Japan's more than $1 trillion Treasury stock into dollar cash without outright sales, but recently published data indicated that Japan had not used it.

Fiscal policy compounds the BOJ and currency questions. Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi defended a plan to channel Yen 370 trillion into critical sectors over 14 years and a two-year sales-tax cut estimated at roughly Yen 5 trillion annually. He argued that stronger productivity and yen-asset demand would improve sustainability and endorsed BOJ independence without opposing an early increase. The financing split between public and private capital remains unspecified, so the plan can support long-run growth while preserving near-term uncertainty over JGB supply and the domestic buyer base. The life-insurance liability channel makes that buyer base more fragile at the margin. Sector-wide payments to customers surrendering policies rose about 40% year over year in the first 5 months of 2026 to more than JPY6 trillion, or $38 billion, as BOJ tightening made higher-yielding alternatives available. Meiji Yasuda's first-quarter premiums fell 28% to JPY793.7 billion. Insurers generally hold JGBs to match long liabilities, but accelerated surrenders can convert unrealized bond losses into a need for cash and reduce their flexibility to add duration precisely when yields are rising.

Northern European inflation moved in the opposite direction. Norway's core CPI excluding energy held at 2.7% in July, below the 2.9% consensus and Norges Bank's 3.3% June projection. Overnight swaps reduced pricing for this week's meeting to 2 basis points from 6, although 15 basis points remained priced by September and domestically produced goods and services accelerated. Headline inflation rose to 3.0% on electricity costs, above the 2.8% consensus. The mix removes much of the case for an immediate increase without settling the autumn path.

Denmark supplied cleaner headline disinflation, with July inflation slowing to 1.7% from 1.9%. China showed a broader deceleration: CPI eased to 0.5% year on year from 1%, and producer inflation moderated to 3.5% from 4.1%. The China policy-bank 5-year-plus bond index gained 0.05%, in contrast with losses across US and developed-market dollar duration. These local outcomes support demand for their own curves, but the divergence also reduces any expectation of a synchronized global policy cycle.

Romania showed that Europe's policy dispersion extends beyond the euro area. The central bank held its benchmark at 6.5%, the EU's highest, after oil and administered-price effects pushed inflation above 10% in May and June. Rates had been unchanged for almost 2 years as political disputes delayed reforms needed to unlock EU funds. Moody's kept the sovereign at the lowest investment grade, while both major assessors retained negative outlooks tied to government functionality and deficit reduction. Romanian local and dollar bonds gained, but the rating relief did not remove the need for inflation to fall and fiscal measures to proceed before easing. Euro-area growth resilience adds a final qualification to foreign duration. A survey lifted the 2026 growth forecast to 0.8% from 0.5%, almost entirely because Q2 GDP rose 0.4%, twice the expected pace. The Q3 forecast remained 0.2%, followed by only a gradual improvement. Stronger realized activity reduces immediate recession pressure, while unchanged forward estimates and renewed energy costs limit the inference that Europe is entering a materially hotter demand regime. The net foreign impulse for Treasuries remains higher Japanese competition and selective high-rate persistence offset by disinflation elsewhere, not a common global bid for duration.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

The common shock was mildly adverse for emerging-market dollar debt. The Dollar Index rose 0.19% to 99.79, EMB fell 0.42%, and the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index declined 0.29%. The combination of higher US real yields, a firmer dollar and roughly 5% oil gains raised the discount rate for hard-currency borrowers, although the moves were far from a generalized liquidation. Local inflation exposure and financing structure remained more important than the index move for the most vulnerable names.

The Philippines illustrates the policy constraint on an oil importer with weak growth. Governor Eli Remolona said the central bank was prepared to tighten as much as necessary to return inflation to target, even after Q2 growth slowed unexpectedly to 2.3% as consumption and investment contracted. Inflation was running at 6.2%, more than twice the government's target, although the slowdown reduced the immediate pressure to act and Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja said core inflation may have plateaued. Local duration therefore faces a stagflationary trade-off rather than a straightforward response to softer activity.

Braskem shows how sovereign association can complicate, but not erase, corporate credit risk. Creditors including Elliott and Contrarian are pressing state-controlled Petrobras for equity, working capital or junior debt before Braskem's August 24 out-of-court restructuring deadline. Petrobras has resisted partly to avoid increasing ownership and potentially consolidating Braskem's debt. Support from holders of at least one-third of the debt is required to avoid judicial recovery, and Moody's treated the existing court standstill as a default. The 2030 bonds traded around 1,900 basis points over Treasuries.

Chile chose an explicit sovereign-capital transfer to reduce a different state-enterprise debt risk. The government allowed Codelco to retain all $2.42 billion of its 2025 profit, the first full-year earnings retention in the company's more than 50-year history. Codelco carried record debt of about $25 billion while production was near a 28-year low, and the retained cash was intended to finance recovery without another increase in borrowing. The company still pays 10% of sales to the state, so the decision trades current fiscal revenue for a stronger quasi-sovereign balance sheet and requires tighter investment discipline. The Braskem case is politically sensitive in a Brazilian election year, yet the relevant liability remains its corporate obligation rather than a sovereign bond. A creditor counterproposal improved the prospect of an out-of-court agreement, but Petrobras's reluctance identifies the opposite transfer choice: protecting Braskem may move leverage or capital demands toward a state-controlled shareholder. Codelco received a defined earnings-retention buffer; Braskem still lacked agreement on the form and amount of sponsor support. The deadline, required creditor threshold and any sponsor contribution remain the operative tests. Those distinctions matter more than the modest daily move in the broad EM index.

## Cross asset

Cross assets validate an inflation and geopolitical repricing without signaling a broad growth break. WTI closed at $82.10 and Brent at $87.68, both up about 5%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 4 basis points. The S&P 500 slipped only 0.06%, and the VIX's 3.76% increase left it at a contained 15.46. The combination fits a targeted increase in the energy and policy premium: nominal activity risk remained limited even as the cost of waiting for disinflation increased.

Technology supplied the more specific risk-off pocket. The Nasdaq 100 fell 0.34% and the semiconductor index dropped 2.94%, with Nvidia down 2.9% after the $500 billion infrastructure partnership was reported. The financing commitment supports long-run capacity demand, yet investor concern about circular funding and a still-larger capital requirement weighed on the equity beneficiaries. That reaction aligns with the credit market's insistence on amortization, collateral and concession for AI-linked debt.

Gold added 2.69% to $4,457.50 despite a firmer dollar and higher 10-year real yield, extending the demand for geopolitical and institutional protection. The dollar's rise was small and remained a 1.17% decline over 1 month, so the session was not a dollar-liquidity shock. High yield also outperformed investment-grade duration in total-return terms. Oil, gold and semiconductors therefore reinforce the central tension: inflation and financing risks rose, but aggregate equity and speculative-credit conditions remained functional.

## Forward Market Significance

Wednesday's July CPI must determine whether Monday's energy shock can overturn the labor-led delay in Fed pricing. The median expectation is for headline CPI to rise 0.1% after a 0.4% decline, with core up 0.2% on the month and 2.5% from a year earlier. An outcome near or below those rates, especially without broad service-price pressure, would reduce the force of Hammack's argument that repeated increases are needed and could unwind part of the 6-basis-point rise in the 2-year yield. A material upside surprise, or continued Hormuz disruption that keeps freight costs and crude near Monday's levels, would connect the energy shock to a broader inflation process and place the September decision back at the center of the curve.

The $125 billion refunding sequence will separate adequate yield compensation from unresolved long-end absorption risk. Tuesday's $58 billion 3-year auction tests the repriced policy path, Wednesday's $42 billion 10-year sale tests demand around a 2.43% real yield, and Thursday's $25 billion 30-year auction tests fiscal duration near a 5.25% close. Balanced nondealer participation and stable secondary yields would indicate that current levels can absorb announced supply even before any future maturity reduction. Tails, dealer concentration or renewed post-auction steepening would show that expectations of smaller future long-bond sizes are not enough to offset present financing needs; renewed yen weakness beyond 160 per dollar would intensify the foreign-demand question.

This week's AI transactions will reveal whether Monday's crowded high-grade calendar and Lambda's premarketing book represent durable capacity or terms-specific demand. Lambda commitments are due Thursday, making final spread, issue price and retention of the 4.4-year fully amortizing structure the clearest leveraged-loan markers. The next data-center ABS or corporate issue will also show whether easier SEC treatment expands supply without forcing larger concessions in outstanding technology debt. Clearing near proposed terms with stable secondary bonds would keep the pressure concentrated in structure and duration; weaker books, wider pricing or post-allocation losses would turn a large investment pipeline into a broader increase in corporate funding costs.
